evidence:
I mapped every criterion (3 gate, 42 functional, 6 polish, 3 visual) to the public notes. 53 of 54 map to a stated requirement or a professional default without adding an exact label, route, colour, indent width, coordinate base or wording; no criterion signs in. Good examples of restraint: cw_block_indent_undo asks only for 'the same indent', cw_mouse_selection accepts a triple click 'with or without its line break', cw_history_restore_retry accepts a stale restore that is 'either refused or added on top', cw_replace_all_atomic accepts a disabled Redo, both format criteria say 'A change of quote style alone is not a failure', cw_live_library_update allows ten seconds against the brief's 'about five'.

CONFIRMED INSTANCE (Fail). tests/scored/functional/judge.toml, criterion cw_find_forward_backward_wrap (id at line 132): 'With the caret at the document start, use the visible Find control and its Next action to visit the three occurrences in document order, then a fourth Next must wrap to the first.' The press count 'a fourth Next' is true only for an app in which entering the search text selects nothing and the first Next selects occurrence one. That is the golden's own convention, not a public requirement: solution/app/src/custom-editor.js:54-55 handles Find input with 'state.query = event.target.value; recomputeMatches(); render();' (no selection), and findNext (1020-1033) picks the first match at or after the caret. The scripted golden test mirrors it (qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-10-02-strict/tests/editor.cjs:193-195: find.fill then 'for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) { await next.click(); ...'). The public requirement is only ui.md:11: 'Offer Find, next and previous matches ... The current match is selected in the editor. Navigation wraps at the ends.' It does not say which match is current after the search text is entered, and policy.md:5 says examples are not implementation requirements. functional/prompt.md:13 makes every listed step mandatory ('A criterion is a conjunction: every step it lists must hold').

MINOR INSTANCES reported for completeness (Note level, not the basis of the Fail):
(a) polish cw_narrow_width_usable: 'By scrolling only vertically, reach the code editor, the Run control, the preview, the console and the library.' ui.md:17 requires only that these 'stay usable without sideways page scrolling' at about 390 px. A phone layout that switches panes with tabs or an accordion reaches them by a tap, not by vertical scrolling. The fail clause ('if any of those five areas cannot be reached') is neutral, and overview.md:3 ('Show the code editor, preview and console together') leans towards a stacked layout, so the risk is small.
(b) functional cw_long_line_editing (id at line 87): 'The line must be shown unwrapped as one logical line.' ui.md:7 says 'The editor must keep a long unwrapped line horizontally reachable', which presupposes no soft wrap, so I treat this as supported; the mandatory sentence is stricter than its own fail clause ('wrapped into several numbered lines'), which would let a soft-wrapping editor with one line number be judged either way.
(c) Several criteria ask for 'the usual keyboard shortcut' for Redo (cw_block_indent_undo) without naming it; ui.md:9 says only 'normal keyboard shortcuts'. An app supporting one of Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z depends on the judge trying both. Not an unrequired demand in the text, a judge-variance risk.
(d) cw_save_reload_restart and cw_stale_save_refused read 'its revision' / 'exactly one new revision'; the brief requires revisions and history inspection (overview.md:3, behaviour.md:13) and a history list satisfies both, so supported.

No configured judge run exists for these bytes; the hosted run in the evidence index was on an earlier candidate and only on the golden, which uses the non-selecting convention, so it cannot exercise the counterexample.
counterexample: A conforming app with incremental find, as in VS Code and most editors: typing the literal into Find immediately selects the first occurrence at or after the caret (this satisfies 'The current match is selected in the editor' more directly than the golden). With the caret at the document start, occurrence 1 is already current before any Next. Next -> 2, Next -> 3, third Next wraps to 1, fourth Next -> 2. Order, wrapping, case sensitivity and literal dot/bracket handling are all correct, yet the mandatory step 'a fourth Next must wrap to the first' is false at the fourth press (the selection is on occurrence 2), and a judge counting presses as written can also read the Next-driven visits 2, 3, 1 as 'the order is wrong'. The app loses cw_find_forward_backward_wrap (1 of 42 functional criteria) for behaviour the brief never excluded.
suggested_fix: Reword the step without a press count, for example: 'use the visible Find control and its Next action until each of the three occurrences has been the current match once, in document order (the first may already be current when the search text is entered); one more Next from the last occurrence must wrap to the first, and Previous from the first must wrap to the last.' Optionally also change cw_narrow_width_usable to 'without sideways scrolling, reach ...' and align cw_long_line_editing's mandatory sentence with its fail clause.
